rule: each mutant must fail its named assertion in each killing test; the expected failures come from the order (H4, L47); each killing test's captured stderr must show the mutated line ran (L41)

m01_f1.what: the shared predicate compares batch COUNTS at equal ranks, not shapes
m01_f1.named_assertion: pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match='^matmul refused: .*batch.*(A [2, 3, 2, 3] on ..., B [3, 2, 3, 4] on ...') -- the mutant accepts the equal-count pair, so the call reaches the GEMM and raises the no-device CUDA error instead (regex does not match)

m02_f1.what: the forward's predicate drops the device check
m02_f1.old:
if (a.device.type != b.device.type || a.device.index != b.device.index)
    return refuse(p, MatmulOperandIssue::Device, "operands are on different devices", a, b, trans_b);
m02_f1.named_assertion: pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match='^matmul refused: operands are on different devices (A ... on <dev>, B ... on <dev>') -- CPU: the zero-element CUDA operand lets the call reach the output allocation / GEMM (CUDA error); GPU line: nonzero host + CUDA operands reach cuBLAS (any outcome other than the refusal fails the regex or 'DID NOT RAISE')
m02_f1.order_source: G5 m02 (G1, mixed host and CUDA operands, staged GPU line)
m02_f1.run: CPU witness + staged GPU line mut_m02

m03_f1.what: the forward's predicate drops the INT_MAX checks (M, N, K and the batch count)
m03_f1.named_assertion: pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match='^matmul refused: GEMM (dimension|batch count) above INT_MAX.*(A ..., B ...') -- the mutant lets the call reach the GEMM (no-device CUDA error)

m04_f1.what: the predicate accepts an all-ones B batch at equal ranks (as a stride-0 broadcast)
m04_f1.named_assertion: pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match='^matmul refused: .*batch.*(A [2, 2, 3] ..., B [1, 3, 4] ...') (and the rank-4 case) -- the mutant accepts, the call reaches the GEMM

m05_f1.what: numpy_dtype returns float32 for unlisted dtypes again
m05_f1.new:
std::fprintf(stderr, "ENG4-MUTANT m05_f1 executed\n"); std::fflush(stderr); return DType::Float32;
  throw py::type_error("tensor: unsupported NumPy dtype "
m05_f1.named_assertion: pytest.raises(TypeError, match='unsupported NumPy dtype <name>') -- the mutant returns a float32 tensor: 'DID NOT RAISE'

m06_dtype_after_alloc.what: the supported-dtype check moves back after the output allocation (the dispatch's final else)
m06_dtype_after_alloc.old:
if (a.dtype != DType::Float32 && a.dtype != DType::Float16 && a.dtype != DType::BFloat16)
    return refuse(p, MatmulOperandIssue::UnsupportedDtype,
m06_dtype_after_alloc.named_assertion: pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match='^matmul supports float32/float16/bfloat16 only: operand dtype <d> (A ..., B ...)') -- host K = 0 / empty-output pairs then return a result ('DID NOT RAISE'); the zero-element CUDA pair reaches its output allocation (cudaMalloc error, regex mismatch). The nonempty K > 0 host pair is NOT a killing test: there the late refusal follows a host malloc (no CUDA call) with the same message, so this mutant cannot be seen through it.

m07_byteorder.named_assertion: pytest.raises(TypeError, match='non-native byte order NumPy dtype <d>') -- 'DID NOT RAISE'
